game: Week 6 HOU@JAX / kickoff not in pack / JAX -2.5 / total 42 / weather not saved

script.base: Book has JAX a short favorite in a 42 total, implied team totals about JAX 22.3 and HOU 19.8. Base flow is a close game JAX leads late by a FG: Lawrence stays in preferred non-blitz dropbacks (HOU blitzes 20%, his EPA 0.37 vs no blitz vs 0.03 vs blitz), feeds Strange/Washington/Meyers, and Tuten still carries the JAX run (54 carries, 218 yards over weeks 3-5). HOU splits the run Montgomery/Marks 26/26 and Stroud throws into JAX's 29% blitz, where his EPA is 0.47 vs 0.02 unblitzed.
script.flip1: JAX gets up early, Tuten clocks it at his ~18-carry L3 pace, and HOU abandons the run so Marks rush yards die further while Stroud volume shifts to Collins/Hutchinson/Noel. Marks under gets safer; Strange over gets shakier if JAX stops throwing.
script.flip2: HOU hangs around or leads and it becomes a 20s slog under 42: both run games stay small against 3.04 and 3.40 YPC defenses, Lawrence's no-blitz efficiency never becomes volume, and Strange's 37.5 is a coin flip on 4-5 targets instead of his L3 pace.

Travis Hunter is absent from the L3 target log; his 3.5 line is not a leg (no inactive confirmation). Tuten 54 carries vs Rodriguez 16 means Rodriguez is change-of-pace, not a full split. HOU: Collins 15/174 and Hutchinson 16/162 are both in the target log, so neither is a confirmed absence; Noel 10/143, Boutte 11/95, Schultz 9/69 are live secondary options. Montgomery 26/68 and Marks 26/99 is a true carry split, not a next-man-up role. No OL-out data, so no pressure or rush-efficiency injury adjustment.

matchup.shell: Coverage charting, MOFO/MOFC, and man/zone rate are not in the pack. Location YPA is the proxy: JAX allows middle 9.59 (29 att) vs left 7.16 (68) and right 7.67 (81); HOU allows middle 9.43 (46 att) vs left 5.41 (56) and right 7.25 (75). Both defenses bleed the middle and are tighter outside, especially HOU's left.
matchup.pressure: JAX blitz rate 29%. Stroud EPA/dropback 0.47 vs blitz (n=42) vs 0.02 with no blitz, so JAX pressure does not suppress HOU passing. HOU blitz rate 20%. Lawrence EPA 0.03 vs blitz (n=48) vs 0.37 with no blitz, so he gets the clean looks he wants most of the day.
matchup.bleeds: JAX run D is the stingy side: 3.04 YPC allowed, only 5 runs of 10+ in 5 games, 17 passes of 20+ on 189 att. HOU run D allows 3.40 YPC and 9 runs of 10+, with 18 passes of 20+ on 196 att. The pass bleed for both is the middle, not the boundary.
matchup.overlap: Strange is JAX's primary target (21 tgt, 195 rec yds, 147 air yds L3) and HOU's soft spot is the middle (9.43 YPA). That is the core overlap, with the caveat that alignment charting is not in the pack so TE-to-middle is inferred not charted. Marks does not attack a run-defense weakness; JAX is the opposite at 3.04 YPC.

edge_players.edge_sentence: Strange is Jacksonville's primary target (21 targets, 195 yards over weeks 3-5) and Houston gives up the middle (9.43 YPA on 46 attempts), while Lawrence is efficient when not blitzed (0.37 EPA) and Houston blitzes only 20%, so 37.5 is short of the role he has actually played.
edge_players.must_be_true: Strange keeps the TE1 target share from weeks 3-5, plays a full snap count (no snap limit in the pack), and the game stays close enough that Lawrence keeps dropping back instead of handing Tuten the clock.
edge_players.kills_it: Houston walls off the middle, Washington/Meyers/a rebounding Thomas steal the intermediate, or JAX leads big early and pass volume never shows up. One quiet 4-target game lands under 37.5, and a single spike inside the 195 yards cannot be ruled out.

edge_players.edge_sentence: Marks is in a true split with Montgomery (26 carries each over 3 games) and has only 99 rush yards in that span (~33/game), while Jacksonville allows 3.04 YPC and just 5 runs of 10+ all season, so 45.5 asks him to beat both his role and a stingy run defense.
edge_players.must_be_true: Montgomery stays active so the 50/50 carry split holds, HOU is not in a lead-and-grind script, and JAX's run defense stays near 3.04 YPC.
edge_players.kills_it: Montgomery sits at inactives (not in the pack) and Marks becomes the closer, or HOU leads and gives him 14+ carries, or he breaks one of the rare 10+ runs JAX has allowed and clears 45.5 on volume plus one explosive.

data_check.notes: No projection model, sim median, or Pinnacle no-vig in the pack, so this cannot be sized to a sharp price. Pack-only check agrees in direction and is not a 70%+ claim: Strange L3 is 65 rec yds/game vs 37.5; even regressing a possible unseen spike still projects the mid-40s to 50s, still over. Marks L3 is ~33 rush yds/game vs 45.5, and ~9 carries at JAX's 3.04 YPC is about 27-35, still under. Tuten rush over 62.5 was a lean and is dropped: 18 carries times HOU's 3.40 YPC allowed is about 61, on the number, so the matchup does not confirm it. Hutchinson over 14.5 and Noel over 17.5 are not legs: L3 pace (about 54 and 48 yds/game) violently disagrees with even-money main lines, which flags missing health or role news rather than an edge.

market_rung_price: Strange recyds over 37.5 at -113, main line, not a short alt. Marks rushyds under 45.5 at -114, main line. No alt rungs in the pack. One market per player. Receptions, passing yards, and TDs excluded by constraint. Rushing under is the market because the edge is a split carry share plus a strong JAX run defense, not an explosive receiving matchup.
pre_mortem: It's Monday and both lost. Strange finishes under 37.5 because the 195-yard L3 was one explosive game hidden in the aggregate, Houston's 9.43 middle YPA was not tight-end targets, and Lawrence handed to Tuten once JAX led, leaving Strange on 4 targets and about 28 yards. Marks goes over 45.5 because Montgomery was inactive at the 90-minute window that is not in the pack, Marks took 18 carries in a HOU lead, and even at 3.04 YPC that is about 55 before a crease. That counter-case is real because there are no inactives, no coverage charting, and no game-level splits, but it is not stronger than the role-plus-matchup read, so both stay leans and neither is strong.
slip_story: One close-game story only: JAX controls the trenches and the middle (spread -2.5, total 42). Marks rush under is HOU's split run getting stuffed by JAX's 3.04 YPC defense; Strange rec over is Lawrence, facing a 20% blitz, throwing into HOU's middle bleed. Do not add Tuten rush over, which needs a run-heavy JAX script that competes with Strange's targets, and do not pair this with a game over or any TD leg. Not a shootout stack and not a favorite-clock-kill stack.
